# MinkExcel

> MinkExcel is a dependency-free JavaScript and TypeScript library for reading XLSX values and exporting formatted spreadsheet reports. It provides a focused subset of familiar ExcelJS workbook APIs for browsers, module Web Workers, Bun and Node.js.

Install with `npm install minkexcel`. The package is ESM-only and includes TypeScript declarations. Use named imports such as `Workbook`, `readWorkbook` and `writeWorkbook`. The application supplies and saves `Uint8Array` bytes; the library does not perform filesystem or network I/O.

Important behavior:

- Import extracts values by default. ReadOptions extends ReadLimits with preserveTemplate (default false). Opt in to retain original archive parts for cell value edits, including formatting, layout, comments and protection. Template mode does not reconstruct style/layout getters; structural and presentation edits throw XlsxError.
- Formulas are not calculated. Supply a cached result when creating formula cells.
- Row and column positions are one-based. Arrays passed to `addRow` or assigned to `row.values` are zero-based; reading `row.values` returns a one-based sparse array. Cell addresses use uppercase letters, such as `A1`.
- Export supports fonts, solid fills, alignment, colored borders, number formats, merges, frozen rows, horizontal print centering and independent lastModifiedBy metadata. It requires `CompressionStream("deflate")` and Web Streams. Import uses the library's own inflater.
- getWorksheet accepts names and one-based numeric positions. Column.eachCell visits populated cells or includes empty cells when requested. actualRowCount counts populated rows; use eachRow or rowCount when sparse row positions matter.
- Import validates ZIP checksums and applies configurable resource limits. See `ReadLimits`, `XlsxError`, `XlsxLimitError` and cancellation in the API reference.
- MinkExcel is a supported subset of ExcelJS, not a drop-in replacement for its entire API. Review the implementation comparison before migrating.
- Benchmark results describe recorded local workloads. They do not establish universal speed, browser performance, streaming performance or peak memory use.

## Documentation

- [Complete self-contained guide](llms-full.txt): Installation, all examples, full public API and types, import limits, errors, ExcelJS comparison and complete recorded benchmark tables in one file. Read this when other documentation cannot be fetched.
- [Introduction](./): Project motivation, design priorities and intended scope.
- [Getting started](getting-started/): Export and import examples, browser downloads, Node.js files, indexing conventions and formatting.
- [Installation](installation/): Package installation, ESM imports, runtime requirements and verified environments.
- [API reference](api/): Current public classes, functions, value and formatting types, import limits, errors and cancellation.
- [ExcelJS comparison](comparison/): Supported API mapping, migration examples and implementation differences.
- [Benchmarks](benchmarks/): Recorded timings, file sizes, methodology, limitations and reproduction commands.

## Recorded benchmark data

- [Bun measurements](data/matrix.json): Recorded workloads, timings, raw samples, file sizes and runtime metadata.
- [Node.js measurements](data/matrix-node.json): The corresponding recorded Node.js dataset.
- [Bun template measurements](data/template.json): Value-only import, template import and complete payroll edit workflow timings.
